chunks: Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the woman whose husband has died, can she go out from her husband's house? He said: She can go out from her husband's house, and perform Hajj, and move from one house to another.

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: The woman whose husband has died (widow)

ai.seo_question: What are the rights and rulings for a widow regarding her residence and Hajj after her husband's death?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of the 'Iddah' (waiting period) for a widow, distinguishing her status from a divorced woman by permitting her to reside in her own home rather than remaining in her husband's house. It further links the completion of her waiting period with the performance of Hajj, highlighting the integration of personal status law with communal religious obligations in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the flexibility granted to widows in managing their domestic life while fulfilling their spiritual duties.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd, from Ibn Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Ibn Bukeyr,f rom Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the woman widowed from her husband, can she go out from the house of her husband?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She can go out from the house of her husband, and perform Hajj, and transfer from a house to a house’.
en.sarwar: 5. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman whose husband dies if she can perform al-Hajj and bear witness for rights. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, she can do so.’”
